from typing import Literal
import mas_operators as operator
from . import prompt as prompt_custom
from scripts.async_llm import create_llm_instance


from scripts.evaluator import DatasetType

class Workflow:
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        llm_config,
        dataset: DatasetType,
        aggregator_llm_config=None,
    ) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.dataset = dataset
        self.llm = create_llm_instance(llm_config)
        self.aggregator_llm = create_llm_instance(aggregator_llm_config) if aggregator_llm_config else self.llm

    async def __call__(self, problem: str):
        shared_memory = operator.SharedMemory(worker_llm=self.llm, aggregator_llm=self.aggregator_llm, num_agents=3, num_rounds=2,
            worker_prompts=[prompt_custom.WORKER_24_SHARED_PROMPT] * 3,
            aggregator_prompt=prompt_custom.AGG_24_SHARED_PROMPT)
        solution = await shared_memory(problem)
        return solution.get('response', "```\ncannot form 24\n```"), {
            "worker": self.llm.get_usage_delta(),
            "aggregator": self.aggregator_llm.get_usage_delta(),
        }

WORKER_24_SHARED_PROMPT = """Solve the 24 game for this input: {problem}

Shared notes from previous agents/rounds:
{document}

Use all given numbers exactly once. Allowed operators: +, -, *, /. Parentheses allowed.
Contribute concise search progress: promising intermediate combinations, corrections of invalid uses, or one final valid expression.
If you have a valid expression, write it on its own line starting with VALID:
If none yet, write brief notes only. Never claim cannot form 24 unless the shared notes already exhaust possibilities.
Do not use any placeholders other than the given numbers."""

{document}

Prefer any line marked VALID if it is correct; otherwise inspect the rest of the document for a correct expression.

```
<result>
```"""
